title: Learning How to Doubt. Part 2
scripture_text: ‘’After Jesus had finished instructing his twelve disciples, he went on from there to teach and preach in the towns of Galilee. When John, who was in prison, heard about the deeds of the Messiah, he sent his disciples to ask him, “Are you the one who is to come, or should we expect someone else?” Jesus replied, “Go back and report to John what you hear and see. The blind receive sight, the lame walk, those who have leprosy are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the good news is proclaimed to the poor. Blessed is anyone who does not stumble on account of me.” As John’s disciples were leaving, Jesus began to speak to the crowd about John: “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed swayed by the wind? If not, what did you go out to see? A man dressed in fine clothes? No, those who wear fine clothes are in kings’ palaces. Then what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet. This is the one about whom it is written: “I will send my messenger ahead of you, who will prepare your way before you. Truly I tell you, among those born of women there has not risen anyone greater than John the Baptist; yet whoever is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he. From the days of John the Baptist until now, the kingdom of heaven has been subjected to violence, and violent people have been raiding it. For all the Prophets and the Law prophesied until John. And if you are willing to accept it, he is the Elijah who was to come. Whoever has ears, let them hear.’’
devotional:
The painful honest doubt of the Christian is one of the things God uses to help us open our hearts up to him. Doubt makes us ask questions about God we would never ask normally.

“Our real idea of God may lie buried under the rubbish of conventional religious notions and may require an intelligent and vigorous search before it is finally unearthed and exposed for what it is. Only after the ordeal of painful self-probing are we likely to discover what we actually believe about God.” A.W.Tozer. faithgateway.com. Accessed 28/07/25

Doubt is one of the things that God uses to strip of us of our wrong perceptions about him, and the wrong theology we may have build our lives upon. The stripping away of our false theology is a very painful, leaving us totally vulnerable. The pain of honest doubt develops our ability to communicate with God. Often as Christians we communicate with God as if He were some advanced answering machine with pre-programmed phrases and clichés, devoid of passion or enthusiasm. But when we are struggling with the pain of honest doubt, we pray differently, there is desperation in our praying, and a frank honesty. This is what God is looking for.

Our bible text looks at the incident where John the Baptist expressed his doubt and how Jesus responded to this.

The Historical context of John’s doubt.

Why was John in prison in the first place?

Herod Antipas, who ruled Galilee at this time, had previously paid a visit to his brother in Rome, and during that visit he seduced his brother's wife. When Herod returned home, he divorced his own wife and married the sister-in-law, Herodias, whom he lured away from her husband, his brother. Publicly and sternly John the Baptist rebuked Herod and called his sin to account before God. When Herod learned of John's condemnation, he arrested John and threw him into prison in the dungeons of the fortress of Machaerus in the mountains near the Dead Sea.

Consider how John must have felt. He had been "filled with the Spirit" from his mother's womb. He took the strictest vow any Jewish man could take, the vow of the Nazarite. He had lived in the wilderness, preaching to the people. He had faithfully declared an unpopular message. He had done all as had God asked, but now he was imprisoned in the dungeon of an old fortress near the Dead Sea. In prison, John must have doubted the justice of God. He must’ve wondered if He had made a mistake. His circumstances clouded his perspective.

Reasons for doubt.

There are a number of reasons why John may have doubted at this time.

At a superficial level Johns doubt was related to his circumstances. John, the very man who had attracted a flurry of attention in recent years because of his ‘no-holds-barred’ announcements of a New World order that was just around the corner. This fiery preacher who shook up everything and everyone with his blazing rhetoric about kingdom come. Here he is in prison where he has nothing but time to think and so John's has come up with a question. But the person to whom he wants to pose that question isn't there and hasn't visited him lately. John’s circumstances exacerbated his doubt.

After the death of his wife Joy, C. S. Lewis wrote: -

“Not that I am (I think) in much danger of ceasing to believe in God. The real danger is of coming to believe such dreadful things about him. The conclusion is not. ‘So there is no God after all.’ But, ‘So this is what he is really like, deceive yourself no longer.” goodreads.com. Accessed 28?07/25

Difficult circumstances can expose our doubts, and wrong thinking.

Although John’s circumstances made his doubts worse they were not the root causes of his doubt.

Root 1. Incomplete information from John’s disciples.

Matthew 11:2,5 “When John heard in prison what Christ was doing, he sent his disciples..” Now look how Jesus begins and ends his reply, by addressing the importance of what he says “Go back and report to John all that you hear and see.” and The good news is preached to the poor.” In other words the disciples of John communicated the deeds of Jesus without communicating the teaching of Jesus. John was told in prison what Jesus was doing, however, he did not told what Jesus was saying.

Patte: - (The Gospel According to Matthew)

‘’Why would people, including dedicated people such as John, doubt and be scandalised by Jesus? This section makes the point that it is because they consider Jesus' deeds without taking into account his words, his teaching and preaching. They take into account only one component of what constitutes the ministry of Jesus… In brief, one has doubts, is scandalised, and ultimately rejects Jesus and his ministry when one interprets Jesus' deeds in and of themselves, rather than in terms of Jesus' preaching and teaching.’’

Seeing God move in great power will never heal a person’s doubt. It is only as those deeds are understood in a theological context, that they will encourage faith.

Root 2. Wrong expectations of Jesus.

John was in doubt because he understood the coming Messiah to be someone that would bring judgement and fire. "'The axe is already at the root of the trees, and every tree that does not produce good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire. I baptise you with water, ...but He will baptise you with the Holy Spirit and with fire. His winnowing fork is in His hand, and He will clear His threshing floor, gathering His wheat into the barn and burning up the chaff with unquenchable fire'" (Mt. 3:10-12).

That was the kind of person John expected; that was the kind of Messiah he was looking for. And here is Jesus, out in the backwaters of Galilee healing the sick, insignificant people here and there, but He was not doing anything to really change the basic structural problems in Israel's life. Rome was still in control, the Pharisees still commanded the religious life of the nation, the Sadducees still were in charge of the temple, and the whole "system" seemed not to be threatened by the good Jesus was doing. What John taught about Jesus was partly true. Jesus would come in judgement, but not yet. Sometimes we are like John, we have some truth, and we put our expectations on half of the truth.

For John his doubt was an expression of disappointment with Jesus, many people do not love Jesus enough to be disappointed with him. John must have been disappointed with Jesus at this time for a number of reasons.

He had taught what he believed to be the truth, under the inspiration of the Holy Spirit, up to this point none of John’s predictions about Jesus had come true.

John was shut up in prison, and we have no record of Jesus coming to visit him, or make some efforts to get him released.

Sometime disappointment is the most genuine expression of love, there is no shame or disgrace in expressing disappointment to God, if it is an expression of broken faith and painful doubt. Sometimes it is the only way we can express our love for God.
prayer: Father thank you that sometimes doubt is the only way we have to express our love for you.
